source: Research/App Store Reviews/5. Routine Planner, Habit Tracker - Daily Time Management for ADHD/reviews.jsonl
body: The free trial version is great, and honestly better than a lot of the more expensive habit tracking apps out there. I’m surprised this app isn’t more popular! A few features that I really would love to see: - An simpler, untimed option where you can just see the current task to be done and check off when you’ve completed it. Some people can find being on a timer distracting and stressful - An option to automatically change certain tasks in a routine depending on days of the week. For example, under an exercise task an option to automatically have “Running” on Mondays and “Weights” on Tuesdays etc. - A timer and icon visual for the watch app - A one time purchase option with subscriptions These features would make the app so much better, but it’s still the best routine app I’ve used!

source: Research/App Store Reviews/5. Routine Planner, Habit Tracker - Daily Time Management for ADHD/reviews.jsonl
body: I scoured the App Store for routine supporting apps. When I found a well-reviewed app that met the criteria I had in mind, I put in hours of testing. I ended up trying out Structured, Habit Hub, Tiimo, Brili Routines, & Time Bloc. Tiimo came the closest to the functionality of Routinery, but it was so glitchy it was unusable.   I’ve been using this app for 2 months so far. It is SO HELPFUL for my executive function issues (late-diagnosed adult ADHD and ASD). Routinery offers the ability to build what I call “routine playlists” (abbreviated as rp henceforth). Some of the apps I tested also have this function. Routinery’s playlists are unique because: 1))) each task in the rp is assigned a duration & when the rp runs each task has a timer (essential for me, because I have time-blindness), 2))) rps & individual tasks can be aperiodic (free from scheduling) OR scheduled, 3))) when an rp is running, tasks *do not* autocomplete until I press the ✅ (unless I select the “auto-next” setting for that specific task), 4))) audio & voice notifications are available at a variety of intervals to indicate the beginning, time remaining, and end of a task, as well as a stopwatch count of time elapsed since the anticipated task completion point if I’ve gone over time on a task and time elapsed since rp was paused (so useful because I often get distracted & completely forget I’ve paused an rp), 5))) creating, skipping & reordering tasks is much quicker & simpler than other apps I tested.

source: Research/App Store Reviews/5. Routine Planner, Habit Tracker - Daily Time Management for ADHD/reviews.jsonl
body: I use this in the morning to avoid getting sidetracked / to start the day right. Some of the useful features are skipping / extending / changing the order of tasks. What would be useful is integration with apple shortcuts (So I can create a shortcut to start a routine), a widget which shows the active task / time remaining, ability to change the order of tasks on Apple Watch and to iron out some of the sync issues (sometimes I’ll skip on watch but it seemingly continues on iPhone and then eventually the watch reverts back to the task I had skipped)

source: Research/App Store Reviews/5. Routine Planner, Habit Tracker - Daily Time Management for ADHD/reviews.jsonl
body:
I love this app, it has seriously helped me get on top of different aspects of my life and implement habits while feeling motivated to complete each task. 

I would make 2 suggestions to improve it:
 
1. Having the countdown visible while phone is locked. Sometimes I miss the end of the task and don’t hear the notification, being able to see the timer when my phone is locked would be awesome 

2. Being able to reorder / adjust the routine while I’m completing it. Getting partway through & realising I need to follow a different order of the tasks in the routine and not being able to adjust them without completely  restarting the entire routine & then amending the settings / reordering etc is sorta annoying. Having the ability to adjust them while it’s counting down would make it more intuitive.

source: Research/Play Store Reviews/49. RoutineFlow - Routine for ADHD/reviews.jsonl
body: I think this is a great app if you need something that will help you stay on task and help you not to waste time. The two features I would really like to see (that would make this app 5 stars for me) are the ability to see the total time spent on a routine with multiple tasks. I only see the average time spent for each task in a routine. And a log that keeps track of the time it took to complete routines so that I can see historicaly how well or not so well I've been doing.

source: Research/Play Store Reviews/49. RoutineFlow - Routine for ADHD/reviews.jsonl
body: Great app: - Simple interface - No patronising & insistent 'motivational' quotes, rewards etc - can run without notifications. Can keep it quiet and track steps with a glance at the screen - no permissions needed - flexible. Don't need a certain start time. Can move back and forth through steps. -don't feel punished for skipping steps etc Could improve: - show total time needed for entire routine - colours don't show up well ie can't see clock well against green background

source: Research/Play Store Reviews/49. RoutineFlow - Routine for ADHD/reviews.jsonl
body: best routine app I've tried, lots of features that work for me like flexible VS fixed routines, allowing some tasks to be untimed etc, and an interface that flows smoothly. I liked that I could pay up front for premium rather than the subscription model.

source: Research/Play Store Reviews/117. Tiimo - Daily To Do List/reviews.jsonl
body: This is billed as the solution to ADHD and neurodivergent organisational needs, but it's really lacking in one area: time recording. What I really want from Focus more than a Pomodoro timer is a thing I can set a title on, then start a timer, pause it when I get distracted, resume when I'm back on task, and when it's over have a total time spent / overall duration with dates & times breaking it down. That would get me past not remembering what I was doing 10 minutes ago.
